sources.citation: Hammarström et al. Glottolog 5.3, languoid page long1375 (refs: Vong Tsuh Shi 2009 [Makuri discourse thesis, mis-attached], Ethnologue 2025) plus reference searches by title (Phuri, Makur, Layshi, Leshi, 'Naga of Myanmar') and author (Shintani).
sources.note: n/a. Only Long Phuri item in the whole bibliography is Naga Survey Team 2006 (listed by Glottolog as a sociolinguistic study/wordlist, unpublished). No Shintani LSTCA volume on Long Phuri (LSTCA has Makuri 2018 and Kokak 2018 only, confirmed in CiNii Books).

sources.citation: Shi, Vong Tsuh. 2009. Discourse studies of Makuri Naga narratives. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xiii+168 pp. [Makury Naga; Glottolog ref 16963, currently attached to long1375]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Payap theses include a phonology overview chapter (tone, syllable, stress remarks) for the language studied; Makuri is Long Phuri's closest relative and the older Long Phuri generation is bilingual in it. Internet Archive copy of the Payap PDF exists but web.archive.org HTTPS was could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker: complete ORCID works list (0000-0002-7304-1685), checked for any Long Phuri / Makuric item.
sources.note: n/a: no publication on Long Phuri or Makuric; his Myanmar Naga work concerns Northern Naga (Tangsa-Nocte, Patkaian) and Khiamniungic.

sources.note: Nothing on phonology; bibliography = Barkman 2014, Shi 2009, Shintani 2018 (Makuri), LSDO 2006 (unpublished), Hsiu 2021.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2021. Kuki-Chin-Naga. Sino-Tibetan Branches Project (web page), sites.google.com/site/sinotibetanbranches.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification only: 'Greater Central Naga' = Para + Makury, Long Phuri; data source named is the unpublished LSDO 2006 Layshi survey. Linked Drive folder holds only Northern-Naga_French1983.xlsx.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd ed., entry 'Naga, Long Phuri' [lpn]. Dallas: SIL International (Internet Archive copy 2019-06-05).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; no typology field. Population 1,000 (2004), 6 villages; little dialect variation; lexical similarity 30-37% with Makuri Naga [jmn], 23-25% with Jejara Naga [pzn]; unwritten.

sources.citation: Barkman, Tiffany. 2014. A descriptive grammar of Jejara (Para Naga). MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xx+245 pp. [related language pzn, not Long Phuri]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing about Long Phuri phonology: Long Phuri appears only as a neighbouring group in the 2004 survey (17-25% lexical similarity with Jejara) and 'Amimi' as a language the consultant speaks a little. The thesis text contains no occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' at all (a full-text search for stress/accent), even for Jejara.

sources.citation: Bruhn, Daniel Wayne. 2014. A Phonological Reconstruction of Proto-Central Naga. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. [related subgroup]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Never mentions Long Phuri; Makuri mentioned once in the conclusion as a Burma language possibly groupable with Central Naga (citing Saul 2005:25, Shi 2009:3). No data on Makuric prosody.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed., entry 'Naga, Long Phuri' [lpn]. Dallas: SIL International (Internet Archive copy 2011-12-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; no typology field. Population 2,000 (2007), Layshi Township; 'Similar to Makuri Naga [jmn]'; classification Naga, Unclassified.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request Number 2007-250: create [lpn] Long Phuri Naga (adopted 2008-01-14). Dallas: SIL International. 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States only that Long Phuri is a linguistically distinct, vital Naga language of Layshi township; sole published source cited is Saul 2005.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Naga, Long Phuri [lpn] (associated with CR 2007-250). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Only phonetic remark: name spelling 'based on local pronounciation, with aspirated /p/ spelled as ph'. Gives autonym Long Phuri, alt. names Longpfuri/Longpfuru/Mimi/Amimi Naga, ~2,000 speakers in six villages, closest language Makuri Naga, no literature or recordings.

sources.citation: Shintani, Tadahiko L. A. 2018. The Makuri language. Linguistic Survey of Tay Cultural Area 117. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. [closest relative, Makury Naga jmn/maku1273]

sources.note: Not Long Phuri itself, but the only published phonological sketch of a Makuric language (Shintani's classified lexica open with a phonology section incl. tones); would give the nearest first-hand prosodic statement for the subgroup if Long Phuri remains undescribed.

sources.citation: Naga Survey Team (Language and Social Development Organization, LSDO / SIL Myanmar survey). 2006. A sociolinguistic survey of Makuri, Para, and Long Phuri Naga in Layshi Township, Myanmar. Unpublished Ms. (Glottolog ref 557638).

sources.note: The only known primary linguistic data on Long Phuri (2004 wordlists from Long Phuri villages in IPA); SIL survey reports usually carry a transcription note marking tone and sometimes stress. Would also fix which villages/variety were recorded.
